subject.title: fix(ssrf): block loopback addresses for trusted hostname origins

question: Should exact trusted-host SSRF policy reject loopback DNS answers for non-loopback hostnames while continuing to allow explicit localhost, localhost.localdomain, *.localhost, and loopback IP literals?
rationale: The patch is coherent, but it intentionally changes a security and upgrade boundary for operator-configured provider origins that may currently use custom DNS aliases to loopback.

options.title: Accept tightened loopback boundary
options.body: Proceed with this shape, treating non-localhost loopback rebinding as unsafe while preserving explicit loopback development origins.

options.title: Broaden compatibility first
options.body: Ask for a narrower compatibility exception or migration guidance for custom loopback aliases before merge.

options.title: Pause for wider SSRF model
options.body: Hold this PR until related guarded-fetch and exact-host trust work share one maintainer-approved policy.

recommendation.title: Accept tightened loopback boundary
recommendation.body: Proceed with this shape, treating non-localhost loopback rebinding as unsafe while preserving explicit loopback development origins.
